purpose: Baseline crosswalk between CYBER_AI knowledge areas and selected authoritative cybersecurity frameworks, standards, taxonomies and technical specifications.

methodology.scope: Curated benchmark, not exhaustive census of all standards, laws, papers, tools, products or national requirements.
methodology.mapping: A mapping means relevance to scope only. It does not prove that the source was read, that the pack covers it, or that a tool implements it.
methodology.depth: All area content depth remains unassessed by this crosswalk.
methodology.types: Workforce frameworks, control catalogs, specifications, taxonomies and research are different evidence classes and are not interchangeable.
methodology.percentage: No total coverage percentage is calculated because no complete, weighted universe has been established.

Bluetooth LE, NFC, UWB, Zigbee/Thread, Wi-Fi generations, SDR and RF test suites need protocol-specific specifications.
SIS safety lifecycle, PLC/DCS/SCADA protocols, engineering workstations and process-specific threat models need asset/vendor-specific evidence.
RAN/core, slicing, Open RAN, SIM/eSIM, lawful intercept controls and 6G research need detailed 3GPP/ETSI releases.
Vehicle lifecycle, ECU/OTA, V2X, CAN/Ethernet, safety-security co-engineering and supplier evidence need jurisdiction-specific work.
Mission-specific space standards, ground segment, TT&C, RF, orbital/physical threats, supply chain and mission assurance need a deeper CCSDS/agency crosswalk.
Facility access, tamper resistance, insider threat, environmental controls and cyber-physical safety need site-specific standards and assessment.
DNSSEC, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS, DANE, BIMI, registrar security and BGP dependencies need protocol-by-protocol mapping.
Fraud typologies, payment fraud, account takeover, bot abuse, trust and safety, and financial-crime regulation need specialist sources.
Jurisdiction-specific legal bases, rights, DPIAs, cross-border transfers and privacy engineering need legal and technical review.
Provider-specific evidence acquisition, ephemeral workloads, multi-tenant boundaries, retention, legal hold and chain of custody need cloud procedures.
Agent autonomy, tool permissions, prompt injection, multi-agent trust, memory poisoning, sandbox escape and evaluation benchmarks need current research.
Key ceremonies, HSM assurance, cloud KMS, lifecycle, revocation, transparency logs and crypto agility need product/architecture-specific evidence.
Crypto inventory, agility, hybrid protocols, interoperability, side-channel resistance and migration planning are not proven by listing algorithms.
RTO/RPO, immutable recovery, ransomware recovery, crisis communications, exercises and third-party continuity need scenario evidence.

cross_cutting_gaps.detail: No jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction inventory for privacy, finance, healthcare, critical infrastructure, telecom, export controls and breach notification.
No systematic search, inclusion/exclusion protocol, quality appraisal or full-text synthesis across all domains.
No verified living catalog of OSS/commercial tools, licenses, versions, maintenance, adapters and operational test evidence.
No exhaustive protocol/platform inventory with editions, deprecations, interoperability profiles and conformance suites.
No cross-domain experiments, statistical synthesis or independent replication evidenced by this audit.
OT, automotive, medical, aerospace, satellite and physical systems require safety cases and authorized test facilities.
No complete coverage of national standards, local regulations or authoritative Spanish-language sources in every specialty.
No continuous change-detection for standards, advisories, vulnerabilities, papers and tool releases.
